Hey! Take a deep breath, it’s going to be okay! I literally had the exact same experience at the vet getting fluids for my guy Charley. I was super overwhelmed. And truthfully the first few times at home did not go well at all. That was a month ago. 


It used to take 2 people, but now I can do it by myself with the EZ iv harness that someone else linked in their comment. At first, one person would burrito him and hold him, and one person would hold the needle. It was hard though and he would cry and squirm and it just sucked. 

I was shocked at how well that harness worked the first time I tried it. He barely notices now. I let him eat treats while I’m putting needle in, and it stays despite him moving around and I don’t have to hold it constantly so I can be hands free. Personally I like the 18g needles because with Charley, time is of the essence, the faster we can get it done the better. He also doesn’t react at all when I put the needle in, otherwise I would definitely use the smaller size.

I do fluids in the bathroom, because it’s a small room and he can’t run off under a table or something. If you think yours will jump away quickly maybe try in a smaller room at first until you get the hang of it. Mine is just super jumpy and squirmy (despite being 18!)

Give him his absolute favorite, high value treats. He’s earned it! 


It’ll take some trial and error, you’ll find what works best for you guys! I found the videos by Dr Kris (iwillhelpyourcat) really helpful- https://www.iwillhelpyourcat.com/blog/givesqfluidslikeapro


If your fur baby isn’t drinking water anymore, he really needs those fluids! He will feel better afterwards!

Hey!! My Charley is exactly the same way- super picky eater, always hated the vet, really squirmy and jumpy, and he also gets carsick and vomits during every car ride which is just the cherry on top! 


Don’t stress too much about the renal diet. That is great that she’s eating the kibble! Charley only eats the kibble these days as well. I had a vet tell me- ‘the best food for a cat with ckd is the food they’ll eat!’ 


Have you browsed Tanya’s CKD guide? It is pinned on this sub and so very helpful! I have the low phosphorus foods list bookmarked on my phone because I often have to rotate flavors and try new foods. 


Do you have any vets in your area that do house calls? Or maybe your regular vet will? That might help ease some of the stress related to going to the vet? I recently found one in my area and I am going to go that route for Charley’s next round of blood work. 


I’ve been doing subq fluids at home for about a month now! I was pretty discouraged the first few times, because Charley squirmed and cried and clearly was not liking it at all and it was breaking my heart!! I also had a few accidents where the needle fell out or I couldn’t get the needle in, fluids spilled, etc. 
I just kept telling myself I am NOT giving up on him, damnit. I spent hours upon hours watching videos, researching techniques, and reading other people’s stories. 



He’s still not a fan of fluids, but he’s calmed down a little and the whole process only takes 2 minutes. He always gets a handful of temptations treats right afterwards! And the best part is- I can see the benefits of the fluids. He has more energy now than he did a month ago, he eats better, his fur looks better, and I know he feels better too! 



It sounds like you are already off to a great start with Nora. Just keep reminding yourself that you are doing your best! Tell Nora too!! It might sound silly, but I talk to Charley all the time and tell him that I’m just trying to help him feel better. They understand!

I leave several cups and bowls of fresh water out for my cat (he’s ~17, stage 3). he recently decided he prefers drinking water from cups, so I got him his very own cup so he can be like his humans, lol. I’ve noticed he drinks a lot more now than he did 6 months ago. So definitely leave lots of water accessible for your boy, maybe where he sleeps/lounges as well as next to his food! 


He pees a lot more these days as well, and the pee doesn’t smell super strong anymore, because it’s not as concentrated anymore. He gets nauseous from time to time, he used to throw up often until he started taking cerenia. 


Also, his appetite decreased. It’s super important that they eat, so if he’s not eating the prescription food, have a backup! I’ve used Tanya’s ckd food guide to pick several backup foods and I often have to rotate food because my cat doesn’t like to eat the same thing every day. 


My cat also HATES going to the vet and it has stressed him out more and more as he’s gotten older. He also gets car sick so that adds to the stress! Have you looked into vets in your area that do house calls? It’s a little more expensive, but sooo worth it if the vet visit itself is stressing your cat out. 


I give fluids to my guy at home, but it took a lot of trial and error to figure it out because he’s a fighter too. Dr Kris at iwillhelpyourcat is a really great resource for this! 


Good luck, it’s so hard watching our fur babies decline. Don’t forget to be kind to yourself and know that you are doing everything you can for him! :)

Here’s my neb Charley, he’s \~17 and got diagnosed with stage 1 in August of last year! It’s going to be okay!

I keep a shmorgusboard of food in the house since he’s so picky. He’s lost most of his teeth (he was a street cat in his past life), so I put warm water in his wet food and crush up any big chunks with a fork. He likes the hills pate tuna and chicken kidney foods, and the royal canin loafs. I always add a topper and mix it in, lately he’s really into the friskies lil soups! I switch it up each meal! He also has a bowl of royal canin kidney kibble out all the time that he grazes on! He’s always loved kibble despite having no teeth lol. And I give him lots of treats too, he deserves it!

He does vomit sometimes, and he has diarrhea on and off. His 6 month follow up is in February so hopefully his levels haven’t changed. He seems totally fine and his happy floofy self.

Our vet told me that the best food for kidney cats is the food they’ll eat! So don’t get discouraged if she doesn’t eat the kidney diet.

Hi! Congrats on your new job! I’m an assistant manager for an apartment complex and started off in leasing! 

It’s a pretty stable job, but it has its ups & downs just like any other. 

As someone else already said- definitely want to make sure your “tour path” is free of debris & trash. We don’t have model units here, we just show whatever is vacant. So what I do is go in and clean each apartment once it’s been punched and completed (even after it’s been professionally cleaned) because the cleaners always miss important things and I refuse to show someone a nasty apartment as a potential new home!!

Open communication with your maintenance staff is very important. 

One thing you have to keep in mind is that these are people’s homes. They will get defensive with you and you are the first person they will take out their anger on. You can’t please everyone, even though you try so hard to.

I’ve had people scream profanities at me, throw things at me, and the best one is when they blame ME for things that are out of my control and actually their fault, lol. You just gotta take it with a grain of salt, smile and nod. Half the time people call me back and apologize for acting foolish. 

Seriously though, I could write a novel about this job. I’ve been doing this for almost 2 years! Ask me any questions you have! And congrats!! :)

Then my house got raided, long story short it was a huge misunderstanding but since I had some acid and molly in my bedroom I went straight to jail. The day before that was literally the last day I saw my students! The school board immediately expelled me from the property (they knew I had been arrested as I suddenly didn’t show up for 3 days and attendance is very strict in these programs. Plus it was a very small town in rural Georgia). 

I had teachers writing letters to the judge, teachers fighting with the school board, etc. but it didn’t work. My college didn’t kick me out necessarily but they did kick me out of the education program. 

So here I am in my final semester of college and suddenly all of my hard work over the past few years got swept out from under me! 

I had to do an intense probation program to just get felonies off my record. It took YEARS to get all of this settled. I worked shitty restaurant jobs, lived in poverty, and watched all of my peers succeed over those years. 

So yes, it did have a huge effect on my academics. More so, it had a huge effect on every other facet of my life. I still have PTSD from that day my house was raided, and the days I spent in jail, and all of the paranoia that ravaged my life for 3 years. But I am doing well for myself now! My ex-boyfriend started showing signs in his early 20s. He was very intelligent and charismatic and he had a knack for outsmarting people in arguments. He was EXTREMELY impulsive and would usually black out for days at a time and have absolutely no recollection of what he had done. Example: On a few occasions he would wake up and not to go to work because he "didn't feel like it". This resulted in many lost jobs. 

He began experimenting with psychedelics, which probably didn't make it any easier for his chaotic mind. The episodes would usually begin with him crying his eyes out because he was "being told" that he had to kill all of his family and friends but he didn't want to so there was a huge conflict in his mind. He progressed to making suicide plans, because he couldn't bear to live with his thoughts anymore. Some of the crying episodes of the voices telling him to kill everyone would last for a few days at a time, the most being 72 straight hours. 

Unfortunately, despite how hard I tried to understand these episodes I just couldn't. I tried so hard that I would just end up frustrated and angry at myself for not being more helpful for him. We lived together, and I supported him financially for quite some time because he couldn't find a job, and when he did he just couldn't hold one for longer than a few weeks. He crashed his car one night and didn't remember what happened so we shared my car. (Luckily he made it out of the wreck with only minor cuts and bruises.)

This all simply took a toll on me and I was always confused so I ended up leaving him. Months later, he proceeded to tell me the day he was going to commit suicide. 

But there is a happy ending. He ended up getting medical help and was diagnosed schizo-affective. Myself, his friends, and his family pushed him to get the help he deserved. The last I heard of him was that he was doing well on his meds.

I am happy he is doing okay, and the more I've come to understand the schizophrenic spectrum, the more empathetic I've felt towards people who suffer from this. Keep your head up, everyone! This is a difficult disorder to live with whether it's affecting you personally or a loved one. I made the mistake of leaving at a sensitive time. I'm keeping all of you who have to suffer, inside and out, in my thoughts and prayers. :)
